newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank seeks to extend share suspension.
newsitem.headline: Maybank seeks to extend share suspension.

text.p: Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) has requested to extend the suspension of trading in its stock pending the conclusion of a deal for the sale of its entire equity stake in Kwong Yik Bank Bhd.
Maybank's merchant bankers Aseambankers Bhd in a statement to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on Tuesday asked that the stock remain suspended for a further 10 trading days.
Aseambankers said the companies involved, Maybank and Rashid Hussain Bhd, were still in the midst of negotiation.
Maybank, Malaysia's largest banking group, is negotiating to sell its 75 percent interest in Kwong Yik to stockbroking group Rashid Hussain.
Shares of Maybank, Kwong Yik, Rashid and its 20 percent-owned associate DCB Holdings Bhd have been suspended since October 21 pending conclusion of the deal.
Analysts speculated that Maybank was asking for 9-10 ringgit for each Kwong Yik share. Kwong Yik, whose stock was last traded at 6.95 ringgit, has a paid-up capital of 327.3 million shares.
Analysts have said Maybank was selling its stake in Kwong Yik to Rashid to raise funds, as well as to meet a Malaysian banking requirement which disallows a bank from holding two banking licences.

If the deal goes through, Rashid is widely expected to inject Kwong Yik into DCB Holdings, the parent of DCB Bank Bhd. The merged bank would be Malaysia's third largest as measured by assets, analysts said.
